033.name: Self-Responsibility
033.hitokoto: Much used in financial administration, it was turned on three hostages in April 2004.
body: "The principle of self-responsibility" first appears in the record of Diet proceedings on 17 December 1952, where a division director of the Banking Bureau of the Ministry of Finance was explaining finance for small and medium enterprises. In 1970 the chairman of the Regional Banks Association of Japan used the same phrase, and in 1972 a division director of MITI used it of petroleum. The collocation was, first of all, a term of finance and industrial policy. In 1991, over the covering of client losses by securities houses, the Director-General of the Securities Bureau of the Ministry of Finance said again and again that it was "an act contrary to the principle of self-responsibility in securities dealing", and in that year alone 72 statements containing the phrase are recorded. Between 1995 and 1999 they reached 586.

On 7 April 2004 three Japanese were taken hostage by an armed group in Iraq. On 13 April, before their release, Yoichi Masuzoe said in the House of Councillors that "going to a place under an evacuation advisory is, I think, self-responsibility", and on 21 April Chief Cabinet Secretary Yasuo Fukuda answered in plenary session that "it cannot be denied that they were not careful enough". The U-Can New Words and Buzzwords Award for that year put "self-responsibility" in its top ten, but recorded "no recipient".

What is interesting is that the first report of the National Council on Educational Reform in 1985 defined "the principle of emphasis on individuality" as "the dignity of the individual, respect for individuality, freedom and self-discipline, and the principle of self-responsibility". Individuality and self-responsibility are twins born of the same sentence, and 2004 was the year one of them alone was turned on the hostages.

made.label: 2004 Into general use
made.fact: On 7 April 2004 three Japanese were taken hostage in Iraq (Al Jazeera broadcast the footage on the 8th) and released on the 15th. In the Diet, on 13 April, Yoichi Masuzoe told the House of Councillors Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence that "going to a place under an evacuation advisory is, I think, self-responsibility", and on 21 April Chief Cabinet Secretary Yasuo Fukuda told the plenary session of the House of Councillors that "it cannot be denied that they were not careful enough. Self-responsibility is … the care any member of society naturally takes."

keyfacts.text: 21 April 2004, plenary session of the House of Councillors, the answer of Chief Cabinet Secretary Yasuo Fukuda: "Close to thirty evacuation advisories and items of warning information had been issued. … It cannot be denied that they were not careful enough. Self-responsibility means weighing what effect the action one is about to take will have on society and on the people around one, and it is the care any member of society naturally takes."

13 April 2004, the House of Councillors Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence, Yoichi Masuzoe: "To begin with, going to a place under an evacuation advisory is, I think, self-responsibility." On 20 April, in a plenary session of the House of Representatives, Yukihisa Fujita said "the catchword in Japan is self-responsibility", and quoted US Secretary of State Colin Powell's remark that he was glad there were Japanese who had taken risks upon themselves.

The grand prize of the 21st New Words and Buzzwords Award for 2004 went to "cho kimochi ii" (Kosuke Kitajima). "Self-responsibility" made the top ten, but with "no recipient". The official note: "It properly means that whoever takes a risk and acts bears the 'responsibility for the result' himself, but lately it is often used when shifting responsibility onto others."

The first appearance of "the principle of self-responsibility" in the Diet is 17 December 1952, in the subcommittee on small and medium enterprises of the House of Councillors Committee on Commerce and Industry, where Hisao Fukuda, Director of the General Affairs Division of the Banking Bureau of the Ministry of Finance, was explaining lending by financial institutions and the bearing of losses. Takashi Ihara, chairman of the Regional Banks Association of Japan, used the same phrase on 3 September 1970, and the Director of the Petroleum Planning Division of MITI on 21 March 1972.

Statements in the Diet containing "the principle of self-responsibility" rose sharply from 17 in 1985-89 to 175 in 1990-94 and 586 in 1995-99. There were 72 in 1991 alone, when, over the covering of client losses by securities houses, the Director-General of the Securities Bureau of the Ministry of Finance (Nobuhiko Matsuno) said again and again that it was "an act contrary to the principle of self-responsibility in securities dealing" (17 December 1991, House of Councillors Committee on Audit).

"The principle of emphasis on individuality" in the first report of the National Council on Educational Reform (26 June 1985) was defined as "the dignity of the individual, respect for individuality, freedom and self-discipline, and the principle of self-responsibility, that is, the principle of emphasis on individuality": self-responsibility had entered the vocabulary of education reform as well.

034.name: Grow Your Individuality
034.hitokoto: Individuality and self-responsibility stood in one sentence of a 1985 report.
body: The day on which "emphasis on individuality" became the grand principle of education reform can be fixed. On 26 June 1985 the National Council on Educational Reform, set up under the Nakasone cabinet, issued its first report, which wrote of "breaking through the uniformity, rigidity, closedness and want of an international outlook of Japanese education, and establishing the dignity of the individual, respect for individuality, freedom and self-discipline, and the principle of self-responsibility, that is, 'the principle of emphasis on individuality'". In the House of Representatives Committee on Education the next day, the 27th, its chairman Michio Okamoto explained this as "the basic principle that runs through all the rest".

At first the first subcommittee had put forward "the liberalisation of education" and "the doctrine of individuality", but the report rewrote these as "the principle of emphasis on individuality". Naohiro Amaya, the subcommittee's chairman, told the Diet that "the content is the same" and that "the doctrine of individuality" was little known to the public. The principle came down to the schools as "education that makes the most of individuality" in the Courses of Study published on 15 March 1989, and was carried on in the 1996 report of the Central Council for Education on "zest for living".

What tends to be overlooked is that "the principle of self-responsibility" stood in the same sentence. The principle of valuing individuality and the principle of bearing the result oneself were, in the report of 1985, inside a single sentence.

made.label: 1985 Emphasis on individuality
made.fact: The first report (26 June 1985) of the National Council on Educational Reform (its establishing act promulgated on 8 August 1984, Act No. 65 of 1984) called for "breaking through uniformity, rigidity, closedness and want of an international outlook, and establishing the dignity of the individual, respect for individuality, freedom and self-discipline, and the principle of self-responsibility, that is, 'the principle of emphasis on individuality'".

keyfacts.text: The National Council on Educational Reform held its first general meeting in September 1984; its first report came in June 1985, the second in April 1986, the third in April 1987 and the fourth and last in August 1987. The establishing act was promulgated on 8 August 1984 (Act No. 65 of 1984).

On 27 June 1985, the day after the first report was submitted, in the House of Representatives Committee on Education, the council's chairman Michio Okamoto said that "the principle of emphasis on individuality must be valued most highly, as the basic principle that runs through all the rest", and Naohiro Amaya, chairman of the first subcommittee, explained that "the doctrine of individuality" in the summary of deliberations and "the principle of emphasis on individuality" were "the same in content", the first having been rewritten because it was little known to the public.

The Courses of Study revised in 1989 were published on 15 March 1989 (Education Minister Takeo Nishioka: "These new Courses of Study were published on 15 March", House of Representatives Committee on Education, 24 May 1989). They took effect in primary schools in April 1992, in lower secondary schools in April 1993 and in upper secondary schools in April 1994.

The first report of the Central Council for Education, "The Model for Japanese Education in the Perspective of the 21st Century" (July 1996), proposed "zest for living", defined as "the qualities and abilities to find problems for oneself, to learn, think, judge and act of one's own accord, and to solve problems better".
The original text of "the principle of emphasis on individuality" has "the principle of self-responsibility" living alongside it: it comes from the same document as NO.033, Self-Responsibility.

035.name: Work-Life Balance
035.hitokoto: A word the health minister called "rather difficult" was a charter within four years.
body: "Work-life balance" was first pronounced in the Diet on 12 February 2003, by witnesses called before a research committee of the House of Councillors. One of them prefaced her remarks by saying that in Japan hardly anyone yet knew either the words or the concept. The next year, on 19 February 2004, when Hiroko Mizushima raised the term in the Budget Committee, Health, Labour and Welfare Minister Chikara Sakaguchi answered that it was "a rather difficult word" and that "the concept is not finished even in my own head".

Three years and ten months later, on 18 December 2007, the top-level meeting of government, business and labour representatives drew up the Charter for Work-Life Balance. The Charter set as its goal "a society in which diverse ways of living can be chosen and realised according to each stage of life", and the action policy attached numerical targets. It was revised on 29 June 2010, and under the work style reform act enacted on 29 June 2018 the ceiling on overtime became a statutory limit from April 2019.

Statements in the Diet jump from 28 in 2000-04 to 706 in 2005-09. It took Japan less than five years for an imported word to turn from "a difficult word" into a criterion of judgement. The year of establishment can be fixed as 18 December 2007, the date of the Charter, but in this group it is unusual to have, from before it was established, a record of the minister in charge answering that "the concept is not finished even in my own head".

made.label: 2007 The Charter drawn up
made.fact: On 18 December 2007 the Top-Level Meeting of Government, Labour and Management for Promoting Work-Life Balance drew up the Charter for Work-Life Balance and the Action Policy for Promoting Work-Life Balance. A fresh agreement among the leaders of government, labour and management revised them on 29 June 2010.

keyfacts.text: The Charter's definition: "A society in which work and life are in harmony is 'a society in which each and every citizen works with a sense of purpose and fulfilment, discharges the responsibilities of the job, and can also, in family and community life, choose and realise diverse ways of living according to each stage of life, such as the years of raising children or middle and later life'." The three states it aims at are "a society in which economic independence through work is possible", "a society in which time for a healthy and full life can be secured" and "a society in which diverse ways of working and living can be chosen".

The first appearance of "work-life balance" in the record of Diet proceedings is 12 February 2003, in the House of Councillors Research Committee on National Life and the Economy. A witness, Joann Sukcha Park, head of Apasionada, said that in Japan "the words and the concept of work-life balance" were not yet known; the other witnesses that day were Nobuhiko Maeda of Ritsumeikan University and Minako Nishijima of IBM World Trade Asia Corporation.

Hiroko Mizushima raised it in the House of Representatives Budget Committee on 19 February 2004. Health, Labour and Welfare Minister Chikara Sakaguchi answered: "I think work-life balance is also a rather difficult word, and the concept is not finished even in my own head."
Statements in the Diet containing "work-life balance": 28 in 2000-04, 706 in 2005-09, 547 in 2010-14, 664 in 2015-19 and 356 in 2020-24.

The work style reform act (the Act on the Arrangement of Related Acts to Promote Work Style Reform, Act No. 71 of 2018) was enacted on 29 June 2018 and promulgated on 6 July. The ceiling on overtime came into force for large firms on 1 April 2019 and for small and medium firms on 1 April 2020.

036.name: Diversity
036.hitokoto: Twenty-one years after management diversity, human diversity entered a law's title.
body: Diversity came into Japan as a word of management. Nikkeiren set up a Diversity Work Rules Study Group in 2000, and its report Back to Basics of May 2002 defined diversity as "a strategy for making the most of diverse human resources". The interim report had been titled Diversity, Japanese Style, but the final report dropped "Japanese style". Nikkeiren itself disappeared that same month, merging with Keidanren.

Local government moved in 2015. On 31 March Shibuya Ward passed its Ordinance for the Promotion of a Society that Respects Gender Equality and Diversity, and on 5 November it issued the first partnership certificate to a same-sex couple. Setagaya Ward began a declaration scheme in the same November. As of November 2025, 541 local authorities had such schemes, covering about 93% of the population.

On 16 June 2023 the Act on the Promotion of Public Understanding of Diversity in Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity was enacted, and on the 23rd it was promulgated and came into force. This is when the diversity of people entered the title of a statute. It has never once been picked for the New Words and Buzzwords Award. A norm that became statutory text without ever becoming a buzzword.

made.label: 2002 The Nikkeiren report
made.fact: The Diversity Work Rules Study Group of the Japan Federation of Employers' Associations (Nikkeiren), set up in 2000, published its report Back to Basics: Directions for Diversity Management in May 2002, defining diversity as "a strategy for making the most of diverse human resources". The interim report of 2001 had been titled Diversity, Japanese Style; the final report dropped "Japanese style".

keyfacts.text: Nikkeiren's Diversity Work Rules Study Group was set up in 2000 and published its report Back to Basics: Directions for Diversity Management in May 2002. Nikkeiren merged with Keidanren the same month to become Nippon Keidanren.

Shibuya Ward's Ordinance for the Promotion of a Society that Respects Gender Equality and Diversity was passed by the ward assembly on 31 March 2015 (21 for, 10 against) and came into force on 1 April. Applications for partnership certificates opened on 28 October, and the first was issued on 5 November, to Koyuki Higashi and Hiroko Masuhara.

Setagaya Ward's partnership declaration scheme began in November 2015 (its rules took effect on 1 November; the issue of acknowledgements began on 5 November, the same day as in Shibuya Ward). As of November 2025, 541 local authorities had adopted such schemes, covering about 93% of the population.

The Act on the Promotion of Public Understanding of Diversity in Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (Act No. 68 of 2023) was passed and enacted in a plenary session of the House of Councillors on 16 June 2023, and promulgated and in force on 23 June. The diversity of people entered the title of a statute ("the diversity of living organisms" is already in the title of Act No. 97 of 2003).

In no year has "diversity" itself won or been nominated for the New Words and Buzzwords Award. Among related words, "biological diversity" was nominated in 2010 and "gender equality" made the top ten in 2021.

037.name: Kizuna
037.hitokoto: In the Diet of 1950, kizuna was something to escape. By 2011, something to deepen.
body: The second sense of kizuna in the dictionaries is still "a rope for tethering a horse or other animal". Its old reading was hodashi, that is, a fetter. Gather the statements containing the character in the record of Diet proceedings just after the war and most are uses meaning restraint, such as "to escape the fetters of the government" and "the fetters of the Empire", along with makikyahan, the puttee. Even around 1980 the main use was "the binding force of law", and the approving "firm bonds" was in the minority.

The collocations "the bonds of family" and "the bonds of community" enter the vocabulary of politics only from the end of the 1990s. The first appearance of "the bonds of family" in the record of Diet proceedings is 2 June 1998, as a quotation from the basic policy of the Liberal Party. In May 2006 the government made a project team of parliamentary secretaries under the banner of "restoring the bonds of family and community". "The bonds of community" becomes frequent in the Diet only after the prime minister's policy speech of 2009. In 1995, the year of the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake, the word was spoken only five times.

On 12 December 2011 the Kanji of the Year announced at Kiyomizu-dera was kizuna. Sixty-one thousand votes out of about 497,000. The New Words and Buzzwords Award for the year also put it in the top ten, but named no recipient. A word that had been a tethering rope suddenly revived, in the year of the disaster, as the word for connection.

made.label: 1998 The bonds of family
made.fact: The first appearance of "the bonds of family" in the record of Diet proceedings is 2 June 1998, in the House of Councillors Special Committee on Administrative and Fiscal Reform and the Tax System (Yuzuru Tsuzuki quoting the Liberal Party's basic policy, "a people that values the bonds of family and loves its country"). For "the bonds of community", the government set up in May 2006 a project team of the parliamentary secretaries' meeting on restoring the bonds of family and community (it becomes frequent in the Diet only after Prime Minister Hatoyama's policy speech of October 2009) (17 March 2009, House of Councillors Committee on Cabinet, Eriko Yamatani).

restocked.label: 2011 Kanji of the Year
restocked.fact: On 12 December 2011 the Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation announced at Kiyomizu-dera that the Kanji of the Year was kizuna. It took 61,453 of 496,997 votes (12.36%), ahead of sai (disaster) with 28,648 and shin (quake) with 26,972. Kizuna also made the top ten of the New Words and Buzzwords Award that year (with no recipient).

keyfacts.text: The Kanji of the Year for 2011 was kizuna. Seihan Mori, chief priest of Kiyomizu-dera, wrote it out on 12 December. Of 496,997 votes in all (the most up to then), kizuna took 61,453, ahead of sai (disaster) 28,648, shin (quake) 26,972, ha (wave) 17,832 and jo (help) 14,011.

The grand prize of the New Words and Buzzwords Award for 2011 went to "Nadeshiko Japan". Kizuna made the top ten but had no recipient. The official note: "The Great East Japan Earthquake, a disaster without precedent, made people recognise afresh the importance of 'kizuna'." Kizuna is also among the 60 nominations (No. 14).

The definition in Digital Daijisen: "(1) A connection between people that cannot be severed; a bond hard to part from. 'The bonds of husband and wife.' (2) A rope for tethering a horse or other animal." It has the verb reading hodasu, and hodashi is an older form of the word for the same rope.

Of the 56 statements containing the character in the record of Diet proceedings for 1947-51, most carry the sense of restraint, such as "to escape the fetters" and "to get away from the fetters of the government", or are makikyahan, the puttee. Even for 1972-81 the main uses are "the binding force of law" and "the fetters of the Empire", and the approving "firm bonds" is in the minority.

Statements containing the character in the record of Diet proceedings stood at only five in 1995, the year of the Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake; there were 37 in 2011 and 14 in 2012. "The bonds of family" appears only from 1998, and "the bonds of community" only from 2006.

On 27 January 2011, before the disaster, Azuma Koshiishi said in a plenary session of the House of Councillors that "the bonds of family, of parent and child, of brothers, of husband and wife; the bonds of local society, of the neighbourhood, the school, the workplace … many bonds in present-day society are at times loosening, at times fraying": kizuna was in the vocabulary of politics before the disaster.

Because the record of the most recent years is slow to be included, the chart goes up to 2024. Statements containing kihan (fetters), kyahan (gaiters) and bansoko (sticking plaster), and misprints in the record such as shin-ban-sen for shinkansen, are included in the count.

038.name: Time Performance
038.hitokoto: Taipa took a dictionary publisher's new-word prize in 2022, the Diet in February 2023.
body: Taipa was in use by 2016, but the date on which it was picked as a new word is known. On 30 November 2022 it took the grand prize in "New Words of the Year 2022", chosen by the dictionary editors at Sanseido. Short for "time performance", it measures satisfaction against the time spent. The selection page explains that it is a play on cost performance, kosupa. It was not even nominated for the New Words and Buzzwords Award that year: only the dictionary side picked it up.

The ground had been prepared the year before. In a March 2021 survey by Cross Marketing of 1,100 people aged 20 to 69, about three in ten had watched video at double speed, and among men in their twenties 54.5%. In April 2022 Toyoshi Inada titled the third chapter of his People Who Watch Films on Fast-Forward (Kobunsha Shinsho) "The curse of individuality and the supremacy of 'taipa'".

In the record of Diet proceedings the word was first spoken on 22 February 2023, by a witness who was a researcher at a think tank; a member used it in April that year, and on 13 May 2025 a Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries answered that "with what is called taipa being valued". It looks the youngest in the group, but as a criterion of judgement that grudges time it can also be placed in the line of descent from punctuality.

made.label: 2022 New Word of the Year
made.fact: On 30 November 2022, taipa was chosen as the grand prize of Sanseido's "New Words of the Year 2022", picked by the people who make dictionaries (1,041 entries in all, 673 different words). It is short for "time performance", the effect or satisfaction gained against the time spent.

keyfacts.text: Sanseido's "New Words of the Year 2022" (announced 30 November 2022): grand prize taipa, second "the X construction", third kimazu. Taipa was also among the candidates put up by Hiroaki Iima for the Sanseido Kokugo Jiten and by the Daijirin editorial department.
Taipa is not among the 30 nominations for the 39th New Words and Buzzwords Award for 2022. The grand prize went to "Murakami-sama".

Toyoshi Inada, People Who Watch Films on Fast-Forward: Fast Movies, Spoilers - The Present Form of Content Consumption (Kobunsha Shinsho) went on sale in bookshops on 11 April 2022 (colophon 30 April), 304 pages. The third chapter is titled "People Who Do Not Want to Fail: The Curse of Individuality and the Supremacy of 'Taipa'".

In Cross Marketing's "Survey on Watching Video at Double Speed (2021)" (conducted 5 March 2021, 1,100 men and women aged 20 to 69, published 10 March), about three in ten overall had "experience" of watching at double speed, and 54.5% of men in their twenties.

The first appearance of taipa in the record of Diet proceedings is 22 February 2023, in the House of Councillors Research Committee on National Life, the Economy and the Regions, by a witness, Naoko Kuga of the NLI Research Institute. The first member to use it was Mamoru Umetani, House of Representatives Committee on Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, 12 April 2023. On the government side, Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Kenichi Shoji answered "with what is called taipa being valued" in the House of Representatives Committee on Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries on 13 May 2025.

Wikipedia has it that "time performance" was coined by Yohei Harada in 2015, but Harada used "time performance" at the announcement of the "an" white paper on young people in February 2016, and an example of taipa appears in an IT company's column of October that year.

039.name: Oshi-Katsu
039.hitokoto: In 2021, as Idol, Burning took the Akutagawa Prize, oshi-katsu missed the top ten.
body: Oshi-katsu has never been picked for the buzzwords award. In November 2021 it was among the 30 nominations for the U-Can New Words and Buzzwords Award (No. 07), but did not stay in the top ten. On 20 January of the same year, Rin Usami's Idol, Burning took the 164th Akutagawa Prize. The novel had been published by Kawade Shobo Shinsha on 11 September the year before, and its author was 21.

The word's prehistory runs a little longer. The nominations for the same award in 2011 included oshi-men (No. 09). Wikipedia goes further back, giving as its origin the song-prize races of the 1980s and a feature on Onyanko Club, but that has not been checked against a primary source. In Sanseido's "New Words of the Year", the editorial departments of Daijirin and Shin Meikai Kokugo Jiten have put oshi-katsu up as a candidate every year from 2022 to 2025. Digital Daijisen, meanwhile, already has an entry for it.

Oshi-katsu first appears in the record of Diet proceedings on 29 February 2024, at a public hearing of the House of Representatives Budget Committee, where a professor at Nihon University called political fundraising party tickets "oshi-katsu, to put it in today's way of speaking". In 2025 there were six statements. It is young to be set out as a view of life, but the record shows it rising.

made.label: 2021 A buzzword nominee
made.fact: Oshi-men was nominated for the New Words and Buzzwords Award for 2011 (No. 09). Rin Usami's Idol, Burning was published on 11 September 2020 and took the 164th Akutagawa Prize on 20 January 2021. Oshi-katsu was nominated for the award for 2021 (No. 07, outside the top ten).

keyfacts.text: Oshi-men is among the 60 nominations for the New Words and Buzzwords Award for 2011 (No. 09), and oshi-katsu among the 30 nominations for 2021 (No. 07). Neither made the top ten. The grand prize for 2021 went to "real nitoryu / Sho-Time".

Rin Usami's Idol, Burning was published by Kawade Shobo Shinsha on 11 September 2020 (ISBN 978-4-309-02916-0). On 20 January 2021 it was awarded the 164th Akutagawa Prize (for the second half of 2020). The author was 21, the third-youngest ever after Risa Wataya and Hitomi Kanehara.

In Sanseido's "New Words of the Year", the Daijirin editorial department put oshi-katsu up as a candidate in 2022, the Shin Meikai Kokugo Jiten department in 2023, and both departments in 2024 and 2025.

The first appearance of oshi-katsu in the record of Diet proceedings is the public hearing of the House of Representatives Budget Committee on 29 February 2024, Kaori Suetomi, professor at Nihon University: "I think it is oshi-katsu, to put it in today's way of speaking" (in the context of political fundraising party tickets). On 14 June 2024 Koji Nakakita, professor at Chuo University, spoke of "oshi-katsu for parties and politicians". There were six statements in 2025.

On the origin of oshi, Wikipedia gives the use by record companies in the song-prize races of the 1980s, pushing a newcomer as their oshi, and a feature on Yuyake Nyan Nyan in which Masanori Ito asked "who is your oshi among the Onyanko?" (on secondary sources).

040.name: Konkatsu
040.hitokoto: Konkatsu was coined in AERA in 2007. It lost the buzzwords award two years running.
body: Konkatsu was born in the AERA of 5 November 2007. Its first appearance is an article in which the family sociologist Masahiro Yamada, on the model of shukatsu, short for job-hunting activity, argued that marriage too is not something that comes to those who wait but something to be got by activity. In February the next year, 2008, The Age of "Konkatsu", written with Toko Shirakawa, was published, and the word spread at once.

In Jiyu Kokuminsha's New Words and Buzzwords Award it was among the nominations two years running, in 2008 and 2009, but reached the top ten in neither. The word settled in all the same, and in 2010 The Sociology of the "Konkatsu" Phenomenon appeared under Yamada's editorship, making it a subject of academic examination.

The state moved too. The supplementary budget for fiscal 2013 created the Grant for Strengthening Regional Measures against the Declining Birth Rate, and marriage-support projects run by local authorities came to be backed with national money. A word put on the market as a personal view of life turned, within a few years, into the name of an administrative measure.

made.label: 2007 Named in AERA
made.fact: The word appeared in AERA of 5 November 2007 (vol. 20, no. 49, whole number 1077), in the article "Preparation: If You Want to Marry, Try 'Konkatsu'" (Toko Shirakawa and Keiko Kimura), as a word coined by the family sociologist Masahiro Yamada on the model of shukatsu, the job hunt.

keyfacts.text: The first appearance of konkatsu is the article "Preparation: If You Want to Marry, Try 'Konkatsu'" (Toko Shirakawa and Keiko Kimura) in AERA of 5 November 2007. Imidas records that "konkatsu first appears in November 2007, from Masahiro Yamada (family sociologist) in the magazine AERA".
Masahiro Yamada and Toko Shirakawa, The Age of "Konkatsu" (Discover Keisho 21, Discover 21), went on sale on 29 February 2008 (the National Diet Library record gives March 2008).

In the New Words and Buzzwords Award it was among the 60 nominations for 2008 (the 25th) but outside the top ten, and was nominated again in 2009 (the 26th), again without making the top ten. The grand prizes for 2008 were "arafo" and "Gu~!".
Masahiro Yamada, ed., The Sociology of the "Konkatsu" Phenomenon: Spouse Selection in Japan Today (Toyo Keizai) was published in June 2010, making it a subject of academic examination.

The Grant for Strengthening Regional Measures against the Declining Birth Rate, which backs local authorities' marriage support financially, was created in the supplementary budget for fiscal 2013 (Heisei 25) and aimed at "seamless support" for marriage, pregnancy, childbirth and child-rearing (later the Grant for the Priority Promotion of Regional Measures against the Declining Birth Rate).
